correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the 20-vertex ordered-pair graph and proved its full automorphism group is S5 from five maximal K4 cliques and unique reversing edges. Enumerated all 1949 nonempty simplices by partial-map choices. Repeated exact Fraction elimination of every signed simplicial boundary column gives augmented ranks (1,19,131,389,421), not finite-field estimates. Signed equivariance is tested for generators on 3858 generator-simplex cases. For all seven conjugacy classes, traces on C_i and invariant boundary images are calculated in exact echelon bases, yielding the stated characters. These agree with the sign-twisted five-letter permutation module and the permutation module on 24 oriented Hamilton cycles minus sign; Maschke semisimplicity yields the claimed rational isomorphisms. Invariant dimensions (0,1) are verified by all 120 permutations and give rational orbit-space cohomology as a ring. The actual verify.py and verification_output.txt are packaged together. No integral lattice statement is inferred.

Neither prior general connectivity work nor the nonequivariant wedge theorem implies the two representations or quotient cohomology.

originality.rationale: Existing same-graph integral wedge-homotopy classification is acknowledged and excluded from novelty; its full statement and proof do not determine the two S5-actions. Full-text classical claw-free and star-cluster results provide only general connectivity/topological tools. Searches of equivalent matching-complex, ordered-pair and cycle-module formulations identify no stronger statement or exact character table. The new precisely scoped representations and quotient rational cohomology require additional exact trace calculations. Publication priority remains a residual uncertainty.
residual_risks: A full S5-equivariant calculation could exist in poorly indexed graph-complex or representation-theoretic literature.
An unpublished explicit equivariant reduction of this same finite complex could imply the character formulas; none was observed in inspected primary sources.
A paper with a general chain model for partial maps without 2-cycles might cover this finite specialization without naming truncated simplices.

value.rationale: The truncated four-simplex is a canonical symmetric polytope graph and the first natural nontrivial case with adjacent nonzero homology degrees. The known wedge decomposition leaves the whole S5-action undetermined. The new result identifies H3 as a sign-twisted permutation module and H4 as a 24-oriented-Hamilton-cycle permutation quotient, an unexpected two-orbit structural distinction that directly determines the nonzero rational degree-four cohomology of the full symmetry quotient. This is a complete natural invariant of the canonical graph rather than a routine known Betti-number recomputation. The claim makes no general conjecture and does not promote unproved extensions.
